hits.title: Add configurable file-output line-ending normalization
hits.summary: Expose a constrained line-ending policy with a backward-compatible platform default, propagate the selected mode from application configuration into the shared I/O service, translate it to the text-runtime newline value, and enforce it at the centralized file-write boundary so all existing writers inherit LF, CRLF, or platform behavior.

hits.title: Prevent concurrent prompt mutation during manual compaction
hits.summary: Use the manual-compaction controller as the exclusive-operation marker, reject ordinary prompts at the shared session entry point before interception, message construction, persistence, or agent execution, preserve extension-command dispatch by placing the guard after that exemption, propagate the thrown admission error through the existing preflight contract so RPC callers receive failure rather than success, and verify the behavior by pausing compaction deterministically and asserting rejection with no execution, in-memory, or persisted side effects.

hits.title: Add edit parity for fields owned by a declared provider route
hits.summary: Extend an existing provider editor to support fields previously available only during creation: propagate the directory entry’s declared provenance into the editor, gate route-owned controls to declared pi-ai providers, populate protocol choices from the owning schema with an explicit unselected state, persist display-name and protocol changes through minimal path operations while treating a cleared name as an unset for layered fallback, then reload the authoritative directory and resolve the provider by stable id before publishing rename-sensitive confirmation. Verify visibility, mutation and fallback semantics, persisted browser behavior, accessibility structure, and shared select presentation.

hits.title: Recover an update safely when autostash restoration conflicts
hits.summary: During an update, preserve local edits in an autostash, pull the new revision, and attempt restoration from the existing finally path. After applying the stash, inspect Git for unmerged paths rather than trusting the apply exit status alone. If application fails or conflicts remain, hard-reset tracked files to the updated HEAD, retain the stash as the recovery copy, report the cleanup and exact manual recovery command, and exit with status 1; otherwise continue the existing stash lookup and drop flow.

hits.title: Harden ordered registry overrides against stale duplicate entries
hits.summary: Trace configuration inputs through registry mutation and first-match consumer lookup to confirm that earlier duplicate keys can shadow a later override. For each incoming setting, mutate the shared registry in place to remove every entry with the same key, then append the replacement as the sole authoritative entry while preserving list identity for existing references. Confirm the resulting ordering and uniqueness semantics; add duplicate-key regression coverage when possible, noting that this episode supplied no such automated test.

hits.title: Surface a failed chat-history summarization at the background-worker boundary
hits.summary: When chat-history summarization returns no response, convert the absent result into a descriptive model-specific exception before constructing summary content, then catch that expected exception at the background worker boundary and report it through the application's user-facing error channel instead of allowing an incidental type error to escape from the worker thread. This workflow improves failure classification and visibility but does not provide recovery: the failed path can still leave the summarized-history result unset and cause a later message-assembly failure.
